subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nature's Own Nanotechnology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Nature's Own Nanotechnology.

hook.text: Lotus leaves repel water with nanoscale bumps. Morpho butterflies glow blue without any blue pigment.

buildup.text: Nature perfected nanotechnology through evolution — millions of years before any laboratory existed.

discovery.text: Gecko feet grip walls using van der Waals forces between billions of nanoscale hair-like setae.

twist.text: These natural tricks are so efficient that engineers copy them — biomimicry is now a booming field.

climax.text: Self-cleaning coatings, dry adhesives, and iridescent paints all borrow from nature's nano playbook.

punchline.text: Nature invented nanotechnology billions of years ago.

quiz.question: How do gecko feet stick to walls?
options: They secrete a sticky glue from their toes
Billions of nanoscale setae generate van der Waals forces
